coverage: All 37 chapters: principal travelers, club members, local encounters, separated railway and maritime personnel, family references, historical and religious allusions.

entities.name: Phileas Fogg
entities.body: The punctilious English gentleman at the center of the novel.

snapshots.body: The English gentleman at the center of the novel, now Aouda’s husband.

entities.name: Jean Passepartout
entities.body: Fogg’s French valet, a former acrobat and firefighter.

entities.name: Aouda
entities.body: The young Parsi widow, daughter of a Bombay merchant.

snapshots.body: Fogg’s wife, the Parsi woman he met in India.

entities.name: Fix
entities.body: The English detective investigating the Bank of England robbery.

entities.name: Andrew Stuart
entities.body: The engineer among Fogg’s whist partners at the Reform Club.

entities.name: John Sullivan
entities.body: One of the bankers in Fogg’s Reform Club circle.

entities.name: Samuel Fallentin
entities.body: The banker who plays whist as Fogg’s partner at the Reform Club.

entities.name: Thomas Flanagan
entities.body: The brewer among Fogg’s Reform Club companions.

entities.name: Gauthier Ralph
entities.body: The Bank of England director in Fogg’s Reform Club circle.

entities.name: James Forster
entities.body: The valet whom Fogg dismisses before hiring Passepartout.

entities.name: Lord Albemarle
entities.body: The elderly nobleman who backs Fogg’s attempt to travel around the world.

entities.name: Sir Francis Cromarty
entities.body: The British brigadier-general traveling to his posting at Benares.

entities.name: Judge Obadiah
entities.body: The Calcutta magistrate hearing the complaint against Fogg and Passepartout.

entities.name: Mr. Oysterpuff
entities.body: Judge Obadiah’s clerk.

entities.name: John Bunsby
entities.body: The skipper of the pilot-boat Tankadere.

entities.name: William Batulcar
entities.body: The circus manager whose troupe performs in Yokohama.

entities.name: Colonel Stamp Proctor
entities.body: The American colonel Fogg encounters in San Francisco.

entities.name: Elder William Hitch
entities.body: The Mormon missionary lecturing on the train.

entities.name: Forster
entities.body: The American locomotive engineer on the transcontinental railway.

entities.name: Mudge
entities.body: The American who owns the sail-powered sledge near Fort Kearney.

entities.name: Andrew Speedy
entities.body: The captain and owner of the steamer Henrietta.

entities.name: The Reverend Samuel Wilson
entities.body: The clergyman of Marylebone parish whom Fogg asks Passepartout to visit.

entities.name: The Reverend Decimus Smith
entities.body: The clergyman returning to Bombay who plays whist aboard the Mongolia.

entities.name: Kiouni
entities.body: The elephant used for the journey toward Allahabad.

entities.name: The British consul at Suez
entities.body: The British official who checks Fogg’s passport and talks with Fix.

entities.name: The tax collector
entities.body: The passenger bound for Goa who joins Fogg’s whist games aboard the Mongolia.

entities.name: The Parsi guide
entities.body: The young elephant driver guiding Fogg’s party toward Allahabad.

entities.name: Kiouni’s owner
entities.body: The man who negotiates the sale of the elephant to Fogg.

entities.name: The Calcutta police officer
entities.body: The officer who takes Fogg and Passepartout to court.

entities.name: The Bombay police director
entities.body: The police official whom Fix asks for an arrest order.

entities.name: The woman at Charing Cross
entities.body: The woman carrying a child who asks Fogg for alms.

entities.name: The Allahabad clothes dealer
entities.body: The secondhand dealer who sells Passepartout an outfit for Aouda.

entities.name: The Yokohama clothes dealer
entities.body: The dealer with whom Passepartout exchanges his clothes.

entities.name: The Indian railway conductor
entities.body: The conductor explaining why the train cannot continue toward Allahabad.

entities.name: The American railway conductor
entities.body: The conductor on the train carrying Fogg’s party across the United States.

entities.body: The man sent ahead from Medicine Bow to warn the train about the bridge.

entities.name: The American train’s stoker
entities.body: The railway worker tending the locomotive’s fire.

entities.name: The Fort Kearney commander
entities.body: The captain commanding the soldiers at Fort Kearney.

entities.body: The older sergeant chosen to lead the volunteer soldiers.

entities.name: Proctor’s second
entities.body: The American who agrees to act for Proctor in the proposed duel.

entities.name: The late-arriving Mormon passenger
entities.body: The man who runs to catch the train as it leaves Salt Lake City.

entities.name: The Sioux chief
entities.body: The leader who climbs onto the locomotive during the attack.

entities.name: The Hong Kong pilot
entities.body: The pilot who boards the Rangoon and answers Fogg’s questions about the next sailing.

entities.name: The Carnatic’s booking clerk
entities.body: The clerk who sells Passepartout berths for the voyage to Yokohama.

entities.name: The Rangoon’s captain
entities.body: The captain of the steamer carrying Fogg’s party toward Hong Kong.

entities.name: The Yokohama steamer’s captain
entities.body: The captain whose ship connects Shanghai with Nagasaki and Yokohama.

entities.body: The broker whom Fogg asks about Jeejeeh at the Exchange.

entities.name: The Liverpool train driver
entities.body: The engineer driving Fogg’s special train toward London.

entities.body: The three priests from the Bombay temple Passepartout enters.

entities.name: The Pillaji priests
entities.body: The priests taking part in the funeral procession in Bundelcund.

entities.name: The Long Noses
entities.body: The Japanese acrobats in Batulcar’s troupe, performing with long artificial noses.

entities.name: The Sioux attackers
entities.body: The group attacking the train near Fort Kearney.

entities.name: The Fort Kearney soldiers
entities.body: The troops stationed at the fort beside the railway.

entities.name: The Tankadere’s crew
entities.body: The four sailors working under John Bunsby.

entities.name: The Henrietta’s crew
entities.body: The sailors and engine-room workers aboard Captain Speedy’s ship.

entities.name: The opium-house attendants
entities.body: The two waiters who attend to Passepartout in the Hong Kong opium house.

entities.name: The bank robber
entities.body: The unidentified thief sought after the Bank of England robbery.

snapshots.name: James Strand
snapshots.body: The Bank of England robber, identified as James Strand.

entities.name: James Strand
entities.body: The man identified as the Bank of England robber.

entities.name: Lord Longferry
entities.body: The young member of Parliament who previously employed Passepartout.

entities.name: Rowan
entities.body: The Scotland Yard commissioner addressed in Fix’s dispatch.

entities.name: Sir Jametsee Jeejeebhoy
entities.body: The wealthy Parsi merchant and baronet related to Aouda.

entities.name: Jeejeeh
entities.body: Aouda’s merchant relative in Hong Kong, a cousin of Sir Jametsee Jeejeebhoy.

entities.name: Camerfield
entities.body: One of the rival candidates whose supporters gather in San Francisco.

entities.name: Mandiboy
entities.body: The other candidate supported by the San Francisco crowd.

entities.name: Richard Brinsley Sheridan
entities.body: The playwright and politician who formerly lived in Fogg’s house.

entities.name: Lord Byron
entities.body: The English Romantic poet whose appearance is compared with Fogg’s.

entities.name: Jules Léotard
entities.body: The French acrobat invoked as a standard of athletic skill.

entities.name: Charles Blondin
entities.body: The celebrated tightrope walker.

entities.name: Angelica Kauffmann
entities.body: The painter cited in the description of Fogg’s composure.

entities.name: Ferdinand de Lesseps
entities.body: The promoter of the Suez Canal project.

entities.name: Robert Stephenson
entities.body: The British engineer who opposed the Suez Canal scheme.

entities.name: Zoroaster
entities.body: The religious teacher associated with Zoroastrianism, the faith of the Parsis.

entities.name: Aurangzeb
entities.body: The Mughal emperor named here as Aureng-Zeb.

entities.name: Feringhea
entities.body: The Thuggee leader mentioned in the account of central India.

entities.name: Ucaf Uddaul
entities.body: The poet-king to whom the narrator attributes the verse used to describe Aouda.

entities.name: Muhammad
entities.body: The prophet of Islam, named here as Mahomet.

entities.name: Confucius
entities.body: The Chinese teacher whose followers are mentioned in Yokohama.

entities.name: P. T. Barnum
entities.body: The American showman used as a comparison for Batulcar.

entities.name: Joseph Smith
entities.body: The founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, discussed by Elder Hitch.

entities.name: Hyrum Smith
entities.body: Joseph Smith’s brother, called Hiram in Hitch’s speech.

entities.name: Brigham Young
entities.body: The Mormon leader who succeeded Joseph Smith, discussed by Hitch.

entities.name: Victor Hugo
entities.body: The French writer quoted about the geometry of American cities.

entities.name: General Dodge
entities.body: The chief engineer associated with the Union Pacific railroad.

entities.name: Thomas C. Durant
entities.body: The Union Pacific vice-president named among the railway’s inaugural guests.

entities.name: Abraham Lincoln
entities.body: The American president mentioned in the account of the transcontinental railroad.

entities.name: The rajah of Bundelcund
entities.body: Aouda’s deceased husband, whose funeral procession the travelers encounter.

entities.name: Aouda’s father
entities.body: The wealthy Bombay merchant whose daughter is Aouda.

entities.name: The queen of Ahmehnagara
entities.body: The queen praised in the poem the narrator quotes when describing Aouda.

entities.name: The Mikado
entities.body: The emperor of Japan, referred to by his imperial title.

entities.name: The Tycoon
entities.body: The Japanese shogun, described in the narrator’s account of Japan’s former government.

entities.name: Joseph
entities.body: The biblical patriarch whose tribe is named in Hitch’s religious history.

entities.name: The prophet in Hitch’s account
entities.body: The unnamed prophet to whom Hitch attributes the annals of his religion.

entities.name: Mormon in Hitch’s account
entities.body: The son said in Hitch’s account to inherit the religious annals.

entities.name: The heavenly messenger
entities.body: The messenger said in Hitch’s account to appear to Joseph Smith.

entities.name: Joseph Smith’s father
entities.body: The father included in Hitch’s account of the founding of the church.

entities.name: The mummy showman
entities.body: The seller of papyrus in Hitch’s account of Joseph Smith.

entities.name: Abraham
entities.body: The biblical patriarch to whom Hitch attributes the writing on the papyrus.

entities.name: Solomon
entities.body: The biblical king invoked in the narrator’s account of Aden’s ancient cisterns.

entities.name: Minerva
entities.body: The Roman goddess invoked in the description of Passepartout’s hair.

entities.name: Kali
entities.body: The Hindu goddess whose image appears in the funeral procession.

entities.name: Juggernaut
entities.body: Jagannath, the Hindu deity invoked in the narrator’s comparison with ceremonial chariots.

entities.name: Brahma
entities.body: The Hindu creator deity mentioned in the account of Indian religious traditions.

entities.name: Kama
entities.body: The Hindu god of love invoked in the quoted description of beauty.

entities.name: Vishvakarma
entities.body: The divine craftsman invoked in the poem, named here as Vicvarcarma.

entities.name: Vishnu
entities.body: The Hindu deity associated with preserving the world.

entities.name: Shiva
entities.body: The Hindu deity associated with destruction and renewal.

entities.name: Benten
entities.body: The Japanese goddess after whom the Yokohama quarter is named.

entities.name: Tingou
entities.body: The supernatural figure invoked as patron of the Long Noses acrobats.

entities.name: Amphion
entities.body: The mythical musician whose lyre could move stones to build the walls of Thebes.

entities.name: The Nizam
entities.body: The ruler of Hyderabad, referred to by his title in the account of India.

entities.name: John Bull
entities.body: The conventional personification of England, invoked in Proctor’s taunt.
